ud6.8:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha, in Bamboo Wood, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
ud6.8:1.3: Then at that time in Rājagaha there were two gangs, who were impassioned with a certain courtesan, whose minds were bound.
ud6.8:1.4: Contending, quarelling, and disputing, they attacked each other with their hands, attacked with clods of earth, attacked with sticks, attacked with swords,
ud6.8:1.5: and there (and then) they underwent death, and pain like unto death.
ud6.8:2.1: Then many monks, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up their bowls and robes, entered Rājagaha for alms,
ud6.8:2.2: and after walking for alms in Rājagaha, while returning from the alms-round after the meal, went to the Fortunate One, and after going and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.
ud6.8:2.3: While sat on one side those monks said this to the Fortunate One:
ud6.8:3.1: “Here, reverend Sir, in Rājagaha there are two gangs, who are impassioned with a certain courtesan, whose minds are bound.
ud6.8:3.2: Contending, quarelling, and disputing, they attack each other with their hands, attack with clods of earth, attack with sticks, attack with swords,
ud6.8:3.3: and there (and then) they undergo death, and pain like unto death.”
ud6.8:4.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud6.8:5.1: “What has been attained, and what can be attained - these two are strewn with dust, for that miserable one in (wrong) training.
ud6.8:5.2: Those who hold the training rules as the essence, or virtue and practices, (right) livelihood, celibacy, and attendance as the essence - this is one end.
ud6.8:5.4: ‘There is no fault in sense pleasures” - this is the second end.
ud6.8:5.5: Thus these two ends promote the cemetery grounds, and the cemetery grounds promote (wrong) view.
ud6.8:5.6: Not having understood these two ends, some get stuck, some go too far.
ud6.8:5.7: But for those who have understood these, who were not in that, and because of that do not conceive (a conceit) - there is no Cycle (of Saṁsāra) to be assigned for them.”
